Two independent identifiers tie this groom to the tree's existing jb_coekelberghs (built from the 1873 SSW and 1903 Kraainem acts): the spousal pair -- his wife is named Anna Haesaerts in the 1838 act and is the same person as the tree's anna_haesaerts, a rare surname (~13 bits) -- and the commune Bertem, stated as his own birthplace in 1838 and as his residence/origin in every later act. A third, corroborating line resolves the one apparent conflict (slagter 1838 vs landbouwer from 1858 on): the SAME man, named 'aangever' (self-declaring father, in person) in two independently drawn Bertem birth acts, is aged 44 in the 27/06/1853 birth of Anna Elisabeth Coekelberghs (occupation still slagter, birthplace stated as Bertem) and aged 48 in the 15/01/1858 birth of Joannes Josephus Coekelberghs (occupation now landbouwer) -- both ages consistent with the 1838 act's stated birth of 29/07/1809, and the trade change happens WITHIN this documented span, proving it is one man's life change, not two men. Checked for a rival: no second Joannes Baptista Coekelberghs married at Bertem in 1837-38 in the Open Archives Huwelijk index (the only other nearby Coekelberghs marriage there, 1 Feb 1837, is Joanna Catharina Coekelberghs b.1797, daughter of the unrelated Petrus Coekelberghs x Joanna Van Brudegom -- a different family, not a rival groom). Chronology holds (first child 26 Mar 1839, 5 months after the wedding -- unremarkable). Confidence: sup for the person record overall (the bridge to Maria Theresia Coekelberghs still runs through the 1873/1903 acts, which are AGATHA/Demogen transcriptions per the project's own §51-52 downgrade, and the 1853/1858 corroboration used here is also index/API transcription, not an image). The parents Henricus Coekelberghs x Petronella Elseviers, and the birth 1809-07-29 Bertem, are what the 1838 act image itself states about this now-identified man.
